summary: The United States has issued a new National Space Transportation Policy focused on accelerating launch rates, alongside updated White House strategy directives prioritizing outer space, artificial intelligence, and undersea technologies. In military space developments, SpaceWERX selected 11 firms to scale defense space technologies, hypersonic startup Castelion raised $1 billion, and a U.S. Air Force flight to Antarctica turned back due to a Russian hazardous space activity warning. Meanwhile, leadership behind the Golden Dome defense initiative touted technical progress while acknowledging funding uncertainties and cost-estimation challenges driven by program secrecy. In the commercial sector, Muon Space secured $250 million to expand satellite production, Portal Space Systems booked a dedicated SpaceX Falcon 9 launch for its Supernova mission, and Rocket Lab successfully orbited its ninth Earth-observation satellite for iQPS. SpaceX also announced plans to attempt its first Starship launch tower catch in a few months. In civil and international news, Japan announced plans to launch a probe to Mars' moons in October, while a proposed private rescue mission for NASA’s aging Swift space telescope was officially called off. On the scientific front, James Webb Space Telescope observations uncovered hidden stars indicating early galaxies were larger than previously understood, researchers identified the Milky Way's fastest known star traveling at 15,500 miles per second, and preliminary research suggested Earth microbes might survive at the lunar south pole. Readers should keep an eye on China’s planned launch of its Chang’e-7 lunar ice-hunting probe this weekend.
